extracted.subtask_description: Reporting on the U.N. subcommission's drafting of a proposed Code of Ethics for the press and information personnel, specifying responsibilities and standards for reporting at home and abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article III — Responsibility for information and comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons engaged in finding and commenting on news assume full responsibility for all information and comments published; if responsibility is disclaimed, it shall be explicitly stated at the time of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopted unanimously by the subcommission (voted 6-0). This is a directive placing primary accountability for published content on the journalist/information person, and requires explicit disclaimers when responsibility is disclaimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article IV — Duty to acquire necessary knowledge when reporting abroad
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons engaged in gathering information in countries other than their own must acquire necessary knowledge about such countries to report accurately and objectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This calls for cultural, legal and factual familiarity with foreign countries before reporting on them; it frames accuracy and objectivity as obligations when working across borders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article V (proposed) — Non-interpretation as justification for government action; moral obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed Article V would state that nothing in the code is to be interpreted as justifying governments to [take unspecified actions], and addresses obligations that news personnel comply with moral standards (text as reported was fragmentary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article was proposed and described briefly in the report; wording was incomplete in the dispatch. It indicates the subcommission's intent to prevent the code being used to legitimize government measures and to remind press workers of moral obligations, but final wording was to be discussed/voted on subsequently.
